_about: IV simulation mode: every clinical number, every step's on-screen text, the three sites' veins and distractors, and the scoring weights (src/core/ivSim.js reads them; src/iv.js draws them). Instructors tune here, not in code. Lengths in mm unless named _cm; times in s; angles in degrees from the skin.
_review: Open clinical questions from the design doc, as built: steps 10-13 run withdraw needle, close clamp, remove port cap, release tourniquet; the tourniquet is above the elbow for the antecubital and forearm sites and on the distal forearm for the hand (the hand model has no elbow); skin prep is an alcohol pad, 10 s scrub and 15 s dry; flush 10 mL, clamp closed before the syringe comes off; gauge gates the vein (minVein); angle windows below.

pain._about: skin: felt once on entry (and again into wet alcohol); perMM: each mm drawn back or swept sideways in the tissue; at flinchAt the patient pulls the limb, taking a loose vein flinchMM with it

steps.title: Find a vein
steps.do: Feel for a bouncy, straight vein, then mark it.

steps.title: Clean the site
steps.do: Open a swab, then scrub the whole circle.

steps.title: Break the seal
steps.do: Open the IV. Slide the catheter 1 mm off the needle, then back.

steps.title: Line up with the vein
steps.do: Point the needle along the vein.

steps.title: Anchor the skin
steps.do: Hold traction until the needle is in the vein.

steps.title: Insert
steps.do: Pierce at {pierceMin}-{pierceMax}°. Watch the flash chamber.

steps.title: Flashback
steps.do: Lower the angle to {lowerMax}° or under, then advance 1-2 mm more.

steps.title: Thread the catheter
steps.do: Keep the needle still; push the catheter in.

steps.title: Withdraw the needle
steps.do: Pull it back into its shield, then into the sharps container.

steps.title: Apply Tegaderm
steps.do: Window over the site, then press each edge.

steps.title: Flush
steps.do: Pull back for blood, then push 10 mL steadily, {minRate}-{rate} mL/s. Stop if it swells.

antecubital.label: Antecubital
antecubital.note: Large, straight veins that take a 20 G: the site of choice for CT power injection, at 15-30°.
antecubital.subject: upperextremity
antecubital._frame: Rest-frame points (cm, tools/measure_palpation.py and measure_centring.py): the origin at the elbow joint, along = toward the shoulder, lateral = toward the lateral epicondyle, outward = anterior. Veins and distractors are paths of [along_cm, lateral_cm] on the skin; depth and radius in mm.

forearm.label: Forearm
forearm.note: Straight veins splinted by the forearm's bones, clear of the elbow's bend: 20-22 G at 15-30°.
forearm.subject: upperextremity

hand.label: Dorsal hand
hand.note: Small, shallow veins that roll: 22-24 G at 10-15°, the skin held taut over the knuckles. It hurts more, and contrast goes no faster than 1.5 mL/s.
hand.subject: hand
hand._frame: The hand lies palm down (PA): outward = dorsal (+y), lateral = radial (+x), along = toward the wrist. Measured on the hand model in this frame (data/palpation.json, centring.json): the 3rd MCP knuckle at along -2.1, the 3rd CMC at 2.2, the snuffbox at (4.4, 1.4), the radial styloid at (5.4, 1.7), the ulnar styloid at (6.6, -3.6); the skin runs out radially at lateral 3.8 (along 4), 2.5 (along 6).
hand._veins: The dorsal venous network: three dorsal metacarpal veins in the intermetacarpal spaces, from the web spaces at the knuckles up to an arch convex toward the fingers over the proximal metacarpals, which drains radially into the cephalic (over the anatomical snuffbox, then across the radial styloid) and ulnarly into the basilic. Hand veins are small (3-4 mm full), shallow (2 mm under thin skin) and loose on the tendons; valves sit near the confluences. Each path runs with the flow, toward the heart.

distractors.label: Extensor pollicis longus (the snuffbox's ulnar edge)

hand._avoid: Where a catheter should not go (INS standards): over a joint, where every bend kinks it and works it out of the vein (the knuckles; the wrist from the carpus up), and the radial side of the wrist, the snuffbox included, where the superficial radial nerve runs with the cephalic vein. A zone is a box in [along, lateral] cm; a joint counts if the catheter's length up the vein reaches it, a nerve if the mark is on it.

avoid.label: The radial wrist and snuffbox (superficial radial nerve)

hand._technique: Laid over the procedure's numbers for this site (core/ivSim.js). The angle: 10-15° into a vein 2 mm under thin skin (15-30° is for the deeper arm veins), lowered almost flat on the flash. The vein: a thinner wall that punctures sooner, lying on tendon and bone that stop it being pushed down far (so a shallow needle pins it rather than flattening it away), looser on its bed (mobility: it rolls further when the skin is let go). The flush: a hand or wrist vein takes no more than 1.5 mL/s (ACR Manual on Contrast Media: the power-injection limit for such a site, whatever the gauge), and extravasation there is about twice as common as in the antecubital fossa (1.8% vs 0.8% for 20 G). Pain: about three times the arm's per millimetre of probing.

tourniquet.do: On the forearm, above the wrist.

palpate.do: Feel for a straight, bouncy vein between the knuckles and the wrist, and for valves along it, then mark it.

anchor.do: Hold the fingers flexed and pull the skin taut toward the knuckles: hand veins roll.

flash.do: Lower almost flat to the skin, {lowerMax}° or under, then advance 1-2 mm more.

tqBelowElbow.tip: For a hand vein the tourniquet goes on the forearm, above the wrist.

tractionEarly.tip: Keep the skin taut over the knuckles until the needle is in: a hand vein rolls at a touch.
